exposure: cesarean section followed by elective myomectomy (CS)
cohort: 243 pregnant women with uterine fibroids during late pregnancy.
finding: Cesarean section combined with myomectomy (CS+M) is associated with increased perioperative risk, delayed recovery, higher complication rates, impaired lactation, and less favorable neonatal outcomes compared to cesarean section followed by elective myomectomy (CS).
mod_finding: CS+M is associated with increased perioperative risk, delayed recovery, higher complication rates, impaired lactation, and less favorable neonatal outcomes compared to CS followed by elective myomectomy.
